#5173. Exodus Reports $8.3M Quarterly Loss as Wallet Platform Expands Payments Business

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Exodus reported third-quarter revenue of around $32.5 million, up 7%, while swinging to an $8.3 million net loss from a profit a year earlier. The wallet company’s expansion into payments and card infrastructure adds a new commercial opportunity but also increases the importance of integration costs and execution.

Exodus built its brand around software that helps people hold and exchange digital assets without relying on a traditional centralized exchange account. Its latest results show that running a wallet business at scale now involves more than downloads and token swaps.

In its November 9 third-quarter report, Exodus said revenue reached about $32.5 million, an increase of roughly 7% year over year. The company nevertheless recorded a net loss of approximately $8.3 million, compared with a net profit of about $17 million a year earlier.

The difference between higher revenue and weaker net income points to costs and accounting items that require as much attention as transaction volume.

Exodus reported around 1.4 million monthly active users and approximately 1.4 million quarterly funded users, reflecting the scale of its consumer product. Those are company-defined measures and may overlap; they should not be added together to imply a larger distinct customer base.

The company also cited roughly $1.1 billion in quarterly swap volume. Transaction volume measures value moved through a service; it is not the same as revenue or profit. The share retained by a platform depends on fees, execution arrangements and the costs of providing the service.

This is a useful distinction across the wallet industry. A product can support heavy activity without retaining a large percentage of the value exchanged. Increased usage can even create more customer-service, compliance and technical costs.

Exodus has been extending its role in the infrastructure around digital payments. Its recent company updates describe a combination involving Baanx and Monavate and a growing emphasis on card and payment services. It has also referenced around 1.6 million active cards and substantial payment volume in the broader business context.

Payment services offer a way to make digital assets useful for routine spending rather than only investment and exchange. But building or combining regulated payment operations brings operational work: issuing relationships, settlement partners, compliance programs, fraud controls and support obligations.

NewsBTC previously covered Visa’s work on stablecoin treasury and settlement infrastructure. Exodus operates in a different part of the market, yet both stories show businesses looking for ways to make digital value move through established financial channels.

Likewise, the growing attention paid to tokenized securities infrastructure reflects a wider focus on how blockchain assets connect with ordinary financial workflows. Neither development should be mistaken for proof that Exodus’s specific payment plans will succeed.

Management cited increased general and administrative spending among the pressures on the quarter. As a company moves from a comparatively focused software product toward a broader financial-services platform, staffing, oversight and integration costs can rise before new lines generate consistent returns.

That does not make the strategy inherently flawed. It means the outcome will depend on whether additional services create more durable recurring earnings than they cost to build and operate.

The useful measures in future results will include transaction and card activity, net revenue retained from those services, the cost of operating the expanded business and whether losses narrow. Users and investors should also pay attention to security, custody arrangements and regulatory disclosures as more payment services are introduced.

Exodus is showing modest revenue growth alongside a more expensive operating model. The next several quarters will help determine whether its payments ambitions create a stronger business or simply add complexity to an already competitive wallet market.

#5170. Arca Opens to Everyone, Paying People for the AI Sessions They’d Otherwise Throw Away

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

After invite-only early access, the desktop app from the team behind Brevis is now open to anyone on Mac and Windows.

HONG KONG, November 11, 2026: Arca, a new desktop app from the team behind Brevis, opened to the public today. Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. It finds the session history their AI tools already keep on their computer, lets them choose which sessions to submit, strips sensitive details on the device before anything is uploaded, and pays for the sessions that are approved. Starting today, anyone can sign up with an email address, with no invite and no waitlist.

Much of today’s knowledge work runs through AI tools. People steer a model through a task, correcting it, throwing out what fails and keeping what holds up. Every one of those sessions leaves a detailed record of real work: the back-and-forth, the dead ends, the fix that finally worked. These records pile up by the thousands on people’s computers, and once the window closes, they’re worth nothing to the person who did the work. Arca gives that work a value.

Arca works with the AI tools people already use, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop. After installing the app, users see the sessions Arca has found on their machine, past ones included. They pick a session to upload, and Arca anonymises it on their computer before it leaves, then returns a quote range. Users either confirm, which sends the session to review, or withdraw, in which case the upload is deleted. Approved sessions are paid weekly.

Arca only reads sessions that are already on the user’s computer, and it lists everything it finds. Nothing uploads in the background, and nothing leaves the device until the user picks a session and confirms. Before a session is uploaded, Arca strips names, file paths, account details and keys, and further anonymising runs on Arca’s side.

“Every AI session is a record of real thinking and real work, and until now the person who did that work got nothing for it,” said Michael, co-founder and CEO of Brevis. “Arca lets people see what their sessions are worth and decide for themselves what to share. We opened it in small batches first to get the experience right. Today it’s open to everyone.”

Arca is built for anyone who does real work with AI, from code to contract reviews, research and long working conversations. Sessions with Claude Opus and Fable, and with the latest GPT models in Codex, qualify today, with more to come. Very short sessions don’t qualify, and every submission is reviewed before it pays. Users can connect GitHub to strengthen their profile, which can raise the value of their sessions, but it isn’t required.

Arca carries the principle behind Brevis’s verifiable computing work into a new domain: things you can verify are worth more than things you have to trust.

Arca first opened on October 13 in invite-only early access, admitting users in small batches. With today’s launch, the invite requirement is gone. Users sign up with an email address or a Google account and can start right away. Arca is free to use and available now for Mac and Windows at arca.market.

Through November 30, the Arca Launch Challenge adds $10,000 in prizes on top of regular payouts for approved sessions.

Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. The desktop app finds the sessions people’s AI tools already keep, lets them choose what to share, anonymises sessions on the device before upload, and pays for approved sessions. Arca is built by the team behind Brevis. Learn more at arca.market.

Brevis builds verifiable computing infrastructure. Its zero-knowledge proving technology, including the open-source Pico zkVM, lets applications prove the results of complex computations. Learn more at brevis.network.

Liquidity in the stablecoin space has contracted rapidly, reducing one of the most significant sources of buying power from crypto markets. Over the last 60 days ending on the 7th of November, according to CryptoQuant, Tether [USDT] saw its market capitalization drop by $6.6 billion.

This represents the largest such contraction since CryptoQuant began tracking this metric in 2022, exceeding a $3.2 billion decline in the wake of the FTX collapse. Trends suggest that investors are withdrawing capital from stablecoins instead of holding them ready for use in crypto trades.

Overall, stablecoin capitalization now stands at approximately $290 billion. With less capital available to provide dollar backing for potential sales and new position entries, there appears to be fewer dollars remaining to fund a crypto market recovery.

At the same time, a decrease in demand of approximately 284,000 BTC over thirty days is evident for Bitcoin [BTC]. As such, if no additional capital flows into stablecoins, then buyers may experience difficulty in sustaining a rally.

As stablecoin capitalization declines, large financial institutions have positioned themselves to capture a greater percentage of the overall market. Project Faro, a joint stablecoin venture, has obtained $270 million from 21 major financial firms.

This includes Goldman Sachs, Citi, Santander, and Deutsche Bank to fund operations over five years prior to launching their dollar-backed stablecoin during the first half of 2027. Still, a euro back stablecoin is expected to follow.

This funding illustrates increasing interest among large established banks regarding participation in the stablecoin market. This is as the overall capitalization of the stablecoin space dropped to $290 billion.

Yet entering the market will be easier than displacing existing leaders. Tether and Circle control roughly 85% of supply, making adoption and liquidity key challenges.

Although Project Faro is preparing for launch, the true measure of success will depend upon how businesses utilize the payment features provided by the project.

As Project Faro aims to facilitate cross-border transactions using dollar-backed stablecoins, they could potentially eliminate reliance on slower bank processing times associated with cross-border transactions.

Companies would be able to send dollar-backed tokens across borders without being required to wait for the standard settlement period. Payment speed and access to funds may also be improved for multinational corporations that operate in various markets.

However, recurrent business payment will ultimately define whether Project Faro achieves its ultimate goal of establishing a meaningful role for its stablecoin products and services as a result of its banking ambitions.

#5166. ARK Invest Trims Block and Bullish Positions as Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Disclosed ARK Invest trading activity points to sales of shares in crypto-linked companies Block and Bullish alongside changes elsewhere in its portfolios. A fund manager selling shares is not the same as investors redeeming money from a spot Bitcoin ETF, and the trades should not be treated as a categorical forecast for crypto prices.

Crypto markets generate several types of selling headlines, but they do not all describe the same thing. One involves investors moving money into or out of exchange-traded products. Another involves a fund manager changing which companies it owns inside a portfolio. ARK Invest’s latest trade disclosures belong to the second category.

ARK’s trade-notification service provides information about purchases and sales by its exchange-traded funds. Reporting of the November 9 trades indicates reductions in shares of Block and Bullish, both businesses tied to the wider digital-asset economy.

Trade data published for the session should be checked against the original ARK notification for exact fund allocations and amounts. Public summaries can combine activity across several ETFs, while dollar-value estimates change with the share price used for calculation.

A growth-oriented fund might sell shares to rebalance position weights, manage liquidity, fund purchases of other holdings or respond to company-specific developments. A share sale alone cannot reveal which of those motives dominated.

For that reason, it would be a mistake to describe ARK’s selling as proof that the manager has abandoned Bitcoin. The sale may reflect a view on the risk and valuation of individual equities rather than the future value of the underlying cryptocurrency.

Block’s exposure to digital assets is also different from Bullish’s. Their revenue drivers, regulation and business models are not interchangeable merely because both are routinely grouped under the label ‘crypto stock.’ Investors comparing them need to look beyond the common theme.

NewsBTC has recently tracked sizable outflows from US spot Bitcoin funds and earlier daily Bitcoin ETF withdrawals. Those figures measure net investor flows into or out of specific products, rather than an ETF manager switching between equity holdings.

Even within ETF reporting, transactions can be misunderstood. Selling shares in a listed company held by an actively managed ETF does not necessarily imply the ETF itself suffered a redemption. Likewise, a Bitcoin ETF net outflow does not automatically show why an individual investor chose to redeem.

Those distinctions become especially important in a market where the same financial firm may own Bitcoin directly, operate a fund holding mining or exchange equities, and manage entirely different technology-sector positions.

Shares of trading venues, payment companies and miners are often affected by crypto prices but can also move on earnings results, borrowing costs and capital spending. A mining company pursuing AI infrastructure may be valued on its power contracts as much as its Bitcoin output. A brokerage might add accounts while earning less from crypto transactions.

That mixture means crypto-equity portfolio changes sometimes convey a different message from spot-token trading activity. They are better read as part of ongoing active management than as standalone signals to buy or sell a coin.

The strongest verifiable facts are the securities traded, the direction of the trade and the number of shares reported for each fund. If later reporting establishes exact price-weighted values, those should be dated and described as estimates where appropriate.

ARK’s trading notices offer a window into portfolio decisions, not a complete explanation of motive. Their value for readers comes from knowing precisely what changed and avoiding the temptation to translate every share sale into a broad claim about the Bitcoin market.

Lumin disclosed that Dogecoin Core's GitHub account ran into billing issues, which she resolved by personally paying the arrears and then switching the billing to herself.

#5164. BlackRock’s SBI Deal Opens XRP Tokenization Question

Home » Trendsetter News » BlackRock’s SBI Deal Opens XRP Tokenization Question

BlackRock’s reported collaboration with SBI Holdings and Startale Group explores linking tokenized funds with a yen stablecoin.

BlackRock’s reported agreement with SBI Holdings and Startale Group concerns tokenized funds and a yen stablecoin—not a confirmed role for XRP.

In her video, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson examines how the proposed collaboration could connect Japanese savings with on-chain investments, while acknowledging that the announcement names neither XRP nor a blockchain.

That distinction matters. SBI’s close relationship with Ripple gives XRP investors a reason to follow the project, but it does not establish that BlackRock intends to use the token.

According to Stevenson, the companies signed a memorandum of understanding to explore connecting tokenized money market funds with JPYSC, a yen stablecoin. No investment amount was announced, and the memorandum is exploratory rather than a final commercial contract.

The proposed work covers technology, distribution and regulatory requirements. Stevenson says other financial institutions could also participate.

She identifies BlackRock’s BUIDL fund as an existing example of the model. Launched in 2024, it held roughly $2.17 billion in Treasuries, repurchase agreements and cash at the time cited in the video; that figure should not be read as a current valuation or a commitment to this project.

The commercial attraction is Japan’s large pool of household savings, much of it held in cash and deposits. Stevenson describes JPYSC as issued by SBI Shinsei Trust Bank and distributed through SBI VC Trade, potentially giving the partnership an established domestic distribution route.

Stevenson points to SBI Remit’s use of XRP for remittances and SBI’s broader XRP-related activities as reasons to watch the partnership. Her central caveat is explicit: “Nobody can tell you that this deal uses XRP.”

A connection between yen-denominated money and dollar-denominated fund assets raises foreign-exchange and settlement questions. XRP could theoretically serve as a bridge, but there’s no evidence that the partners have selected it.

In a nutshell, the meaningful milestones are a named blockchain, disclosed settlement arrangements and an actual product launch.

Tokenized fund distribution could expand without generating demand for XRP; SBI’s involvement alone is not evidence of token adoption.

#5162. Binance Hack Launderers Mint Elon Musk and Animal Meme Coins to Move Stolen Crypto

Binance Hack Launderers Mint Elon Musk and Animal Meme Coins to Move Stolen Crypto

North Korea’s hackers have found a novel use for the internet’s favorite joke tokens: laundering a slice of the record $6.4 billion stolen from Binance.

According to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, the launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and using them to shuffle stolen funds through decentralized exchanges in a way that breaks the direct onchain link between the thief’s wallet and the one collecting the proceeds.

The launderers mint a brand-new token, pair it with a real asset like Near or a stablecoin in a liquidity pool, pay stolen funds into the pool through one set of wallets to buy the token, then sell it back through a separate set of wallets to withdraw clean-looking assets.

Because the pool sits in the middle, no stolen funds move directly from the buying wallet to the collecting one, and the receiving wallets look like ordinary traders cashing out a meme coin.

Elliptic, in research credited to co-founder Tom Robinson, said the launderers deployed the tactic on Tron and Near, with a close variant on Solana. The clearest example came on Near, where between Nov. 5 and 7 they created at least six home-made tokens, each paired with Near in its own pool.

The coins carried the usual meme-coin trappings: cartoon logos of a bow-wearing monkey, a flag-draped duck, a chimpanzee and a fox, one even featuring an “Elon 2028 President” image of Elon Musk, who has no connection to the tokens. The names ran from the crude (FUK) to a riff on dog coins (SINU).

Each token cost about 25 Near tokens, roughly $90, to create. All six followed the same arc: launched, traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR, then abandoned, with the leftover liquidity pulled on Nov. 8.

In total, about 117,000 Near, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens before much of it flowed into stablecoins or a cross-chain bridge.

The sums are modest so far, a reminder that the bulk of the haul is still parked onchain. Elliptic earlier found more than $3 billion of the stolen crypto had yet to be laundered, and that the launderers were spinning up a new wallet roughly every 25 seconds to move funds at machine speed.

Crucially, the meme-coin trick doesn’t actually hide the money. Elliptic stressed the trail remains fully traceable onchain; the maneuver only slows investigators down, buying time in what is essentially a race to move funds before they get flagged.

It’s one cheap, disposable layer among many that North Korea’s launderers stack together. Elliptic first observed the tactic last year while tracing the $1.5 billion Bybit theft, also attributed to the TraderTraitor group behind the Binance breach.

For compliance teams, the firm warned, funds arriving from a liquidity pool shouldn’t be assumed clean, especially where freshly minted tokens and a handful of trading wallets are involved.

The appointment follows the launch of Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain mainnet and AI agent services, backed by $45 million in founder funding.

SAN FRANCISCO, November 11, 2026 — Phase, a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, today announced that Yana Prikhodchenko, former CEO of Cointelegraph, has joined the company as co-founder and CEO. She will lead strategy, global expansion and commercial development, working alongside founder Kirill Eves, as Phase scales its decentralized infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

Prikhodchenko joins Phase after nearly five years at Cointelegraph, where she served as CEO, leading a global team of more than 200 people and transforming the company from a crypto news platform into a diversified group spanning media, marketing, research, acceleration and industry events. Before joining Cointelegraph, she spent more than a decade in senior leadership roles at major banking and insurance companies, including Allianz.

Phase is building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, giving AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. These services run on Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices whose owners earn rewards for validating transactions and contributing connectivity and computing power.

“AI agents are moving from answering questions to performing real tasks on our behalf, but the infrastructure they depend on was not built for autonomous systems. Phase is building an open, decentralized network that anyone can participate in. My focus is to bring this technology to developers and businesses worldwide and build the ecosystem needed to support the next generation of AI agents,” said Yana Prikhodchenko, co-founder and CEO of Phase.

“Yana brings extensive leadership experience across media, technology and financial services, along with the operational expertise and industry relationships needed to take Phase into its next stage of growth. As we bring our technology to market, she will lead the company’s commercial development and global expansion,” said Kirill Eves, founder of Phase.

Phase is a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, with four integrated services that give AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. The platform runs on its own Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices. Phase has received $45 million in funding from its founder, Kirill Eves.

Phase Proxy enables AI agents acting on behalf of users to access websites that restrict automated traffic through mobile and residential internet connections. Phase Router intelligently directs requests across leading AI models to optimize quality, performance and cost. Phase Compute harnesses the processing power of devices across the network to run open-weight AI models, while on-chain settlement enables autonomous payments using stablecoins and PHASE, the network’s native token. Phase is building its own AI model to serve as the platform’s central intelligence, capable of advanced reasoning, solving complex tasks independently and orchestrating other AI models.

Unlike most blockchain networks that require dedicated servers or token staking, Phase allows anyone to become a validator simply by downloading the app, without specialized hardware or upfront investment. Its reputation-based consensus and randomized validator selection secure the network and prevent control from concentrating in the hands of a few powerful operators. Phase rewards device owners with PHASE tokens for validating blocks and contributing connectivity and computing power, enabling millions of people to help build the AI economy and share in the value it creates.

#5157. Bitcoin Core Breaks Silence on Three Patched Security Vulnerabilities

Bitcoin Core developers have revealed three key security vulnerabilities, including a high-severity flaw that could potentially disrupt the mining capabilities of the Bitcoin network, preventing miners from creating new blocks.

As revealed in security advisories published on Nov. 10, the vulnerabilities impacted various elements of the Bitcoin Core software that powers many nodes underpinning the world's leading cryptocurrency.

One of the vulnerabilities, titled CVE-2025-62861, was rated as a high-severity issue due to its potential effect on Bitcoin miners.

The bug has the potential to create problems after a blockchain reorganization, which is when previously accepted blocks are replaced by the network with an alternative chain.

More precisely, the issue could cause an inconsistent state in the node's mempool, where all unconfirmed transactions are stored.

The vulnerability impacted Bitcoin Core software versions 28.0-28.2 and 29.0-29.1.

It was first reported on Sept. 26, 2025, by security researcher Niklas Goegge.

Beyond the mining vulnerability, Bitcoin Core developers have announced two further security problems, rated medium severity.

The first one (CVE-2025-62859) could enable malicious network participants to slow down Bitcoin block processing through an exploit that involves changes in transaction witness data.

Under some circumstances, it could make an affected node wait for up to 10 minutes before processing a block.

Moreover, such an attack could be repeated indefinitely on the node when the latter is running in specific configurations.

The vulnerability was found by Eugene Siegel in April 2025.

The second vulnerability (CVE-2025-62860) involved Bitcoin nodes that operate on the anonymous Tor network.

In fact, the Bitcoin Core developers revealed that thousands of reachable Bitcoin mainnet nodes had been granting permissions for incoming Tor connections.

Nevertheless, the issue did not affect nodes that do not use the optional whitelist configuration.

The three vulnerabilities are not new discoveries.

In fact, all of the issues were already fixed by the Bitcoin Core developers in October 2025.

The fixes were integrated into both Bitcoin Core 30.0, which was released on Oct. 10, and Bitcoin Core 29.2, rolled out on Oct. 14.

The high-severity mining vulnerability was also patched in Bitcoin Core 28.3.

The delay in the disclosure of the vulnerabilities was in line with the Bitcoin Core security policy, which usually calls for developers to wait at least two weeks after the end of life of the last affected software version before publishing details of medium- or high-severity vulnerabilities.

#5156. Google Takes Aim at Nvidia With New AI Chips Built for Privacy and Massive Memory

The TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max join Google’s eighth-generation Tensor Processing Unit lineup, giving businesses four configurations for training and running AI models. Google says it serves nearly 100 TPU customers, from AI labs to universities.

Unlike Nvidia’s widely used graphics processing units, TPUs are purpose-built AI accelerators. Google developed them for its own services but increasingly sells access to outside companies, including on-premises customers.

“With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows,” wrote Amin Vahdat, Google’s chief technologist and senior vice president of AI and infrastructure, in Google's announcement.

TPU 8tx targets a problem that many serious businesses have when it comes to adopting AI: protecting sensitive information while a model is using it.

Data is encrypted in storage and during transmission, but processing typically requires decrypting it in memory. Google says the configuration uses hardware-level confidential computing to isolate customer data and proprietary model parameters even during operation.

The system combines TPU 8t silicon with fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors and Google’s low-latency Boardfly network. Google claims it can cut latency by up to half versus TPU 8t, with almost no performance penalty for the added protection.

Companies could fine-tune and run models on the same system instead of transferring sensitive information between clusters. However, confidential computing cannot prevent a poorly designed AI agent from mishandling data it is allowed to access.

TPU 8i Max addresses another limitation: memory. Autonomous agents analyzing data, codebases, documents or hours of video, etc; need fast access to far more information than conventional AI tasks.

Google combines two TPU 8i chips into one package, doubling computing power, on-chip SRAM and high-bandwidth memory throughput versus TPU 8i. The design packs twice as much silicon into the same rack footprint.

“Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall,” Vahdat wrote.

Google is open-sourcing TPU Sync, software that moves AI working memory between chips, servers and storage. It claims the system can reduce certain data-transfer delays and response startup times by more than 90%.

Google's announcement comes as Nvidia faces mounting pressure on Wall Street. Shares plunged 9.3% on Thursday and fell another 5% in Monday's trading after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for China. Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation, although the company says it has no evidence that corporate secrets were compromised.

The scandal adds to concerns about Nvidia's growth as competitors target its AI chip dominance. OpenAI is reportedly planning to purchase Google's TPUs to reduce its reliance on Nvidia. This is still unconfirmed, but Google's expanding chip lineup could give AI developers more bargaining power, threatening Nvidia's market share and future growth expectations.

Google is competing on specialized hardware and software, not just chip speed. Its open-source TorchTPU project also lets developers run PyTorch and Hugging Face models on TPUs without rewriting their applications.

Still, Google’s performance figures compare its new systems with earlier Google hardware, not Nvidia’s latest products. The company did not disclose pricing or availability dates for the two new configurations.

Ripple-backed XRP treasury company Evernorth Holdings (XRPN) is under extreme pressure as its shares have declined by over 40% while big investors like Ripple Labs move closer to potentially selling millions of shares.

Earlier this week, Evernorth filed a prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), indicating that the XRP-focused company has registered a whopping 73,688,162 Class A shares for potential resale by existing shareholders.

Evernorth's prospectus comes as the XRP-focused company is enduring a brutal stock market debut. XRPN began trading on Nasdaq on Oct. 12.

On Nov. 10, Evernorth's stock price dropped 23.54%. XRPN ended the day at $7.96, compared to $10.41 in the previous trading session. Moreover, about 1.39 million shares were traded, which is a significant jump from about 369,000 shares on Nov. 9.

So far, Evernorth's share price has declined by around 48% from its closing price on Oct. 28 ($15.26). The magnitude of the decline is even greater if we consider the high share price on its debut day ($19.39). XRPN's stock price is down by around 59% from that high.

Some of the biggest names and companies linked to the XRP ecosystem are shareholders who have registered shares for potential sale, as per the prospectus filed with the SEC.

Similarly, the second-largest shareholder is Ripple Labs, which has about 18.14 million shares registered. Then there are various entities linked to SBI Holdings, a big Japanese financial institution. They have 11.79 million shares registered, as per the prospectus filed with the SEC.

It is important to understand that the fact that they've registered shares for sale doesn't mean that these investors have sold their holdings or necessarily plan to sell them.

#5152. Hoskinson says he cannot run Cardano like a CEO. Who is accountable for its growth?

DReps approve spending, while recipients and administrators answer for funded work that ADA holders can trace through public reports.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson said around 28 minutes into his Nov. 7 AMA that he did not control Cardano's treasury or consensus and could not negotiate on behalf of all ADA holders. His argument that he cannot act as the ecosystem's CEO puts a practical question back before holders: who answers for the work meant to grow Cardano?

The answer depends on the decision. Delegated representatives, or DReps, approve treasury spending, the Constitutional Committee checks constitutionality, and funded recipients deliver under the terms of their proposals. Named administrators must monitor fund use and ensure deliverables are achieved. Cardano's treasury guidance explicitly separates approval from reporting on payouts and results.

Anyone can propose a treasury withdrawal. It needs DRep and Constitutional Committee approval, must comply with the Constitution and must remain within the applicable Net Change Limit, the cap on how much ADA can leave the treasury during a period.

Those roles answer different questions. DReps decide whether to support funding. The committee's mandate is limited to constitutionality; it must operate transparently and publish its decisions.

The Constitution's treasury standards require proposals to state their purpose, delivery period, costs and refund circumstances, and disclose whether the prospective recipient received treasury ADA in the previous 24 months.

Funding requests must also allocate ADA for periodic independent audits and oversight metrics, and designate administrators responsible for monitoring spending and ensuring delivery. While an administrator holds withdrawn funds before disbursement, they must remain in separate accounts the community can audit, with the Constitution's restrictions on delegation.

Two approval roles authorize funding. Recipients and named administrators carry distinct responsibilities for delivery and oversight.

Intersect's November 6 update reports that AdaStat's October maintenance milestone was signed off November 2.

The November 3 consensus report maps code and prototype work to funded Initiative 4. The November 6 report keeps it at development, not mainnet release.

Follow the funding decision to the promised work, its administrator and the public delivery record.

The charter describes obligations, not verified compliance across all projects. AdaStat acceptance is attributed to Intersect. Leios remains development work in the November 6 report. Neither example measures ecosystem-wide adoption.

Qualitative responsibility map from current rules, with a selectable comparison of dated public reports. Lines show approval dependencies and monitoring duties, not money amounts, voting weight, a payout order or elapsed time. No calculations or forecasts.

The charter describes obligations, not verified compliance across all projects. AdaStat acceptance is attributed to Intersect. Leios remains development work in the November 6 report. Neither example measures ecosystem-wide adoption.

Cardano's accountability guidance adds a practical benchmark: open milestone reports, published spending, delivery of the proposed work and return of unused funds where applicable. These expectations help holders judge performance. The requirement to fund an audit, however, is distinct from evidence that a particular audit has happened; refund conditions also depend on the approved terms.

A recent example comes from AdaStat, a Cardano explorer. In its Nov. 6 delivery-assurance update, the Cardano organization Intersect reported that AdaStat's October maintenance milestone was signed off on Nov. 2. According to that account, AdaStat reported security, error-handling, recovery and usability work.

Engineering reports offer another view. The consensus team's Nov. 3 update maps Leios implementation and prototype work to Treasury Funding Initiative 4, and maintenance to Initiative 17. It links code changes and releases, giving readers concrete outputs to inspect alongside the funded scope.

The deployment boundary matters. The Nov. 6 development report says the latest Leios changes on the main development branch remain development work rather than a mainnet release.

Hoskinson remains CEO and founder of Input Output Group, according to its leadership page. His AMA presented building applications as his route to bringing people into Cardano. Later, around 2:19 into the broadcast, he distinguished speaking to his audience personally from speaking as Cardano's CEO.

Delivery responsibility is also spreading across organizations. IO announced Nov. 5 that consensus engineering would move to the firm Serokell and developer experience to AlwaysTrue, with engineers accompanying their work. The moves follow separate schedules through early 2027, with public coordination through Intersect.

Holders also retain a governance response: they can register as DReps, delegate their voting stake to a DRep or change that voting delegation. That gives them a way to act on funding decisions and voting records. Growth still has to emerge from the work those decisions support, and the meaningful test is whether promised outputs become usable products and services.

#5151. AI Data Centers Are Buying Used Jet Engines as New Power Turbines Take Six Years

AI Data Centers Are Buying Used Jet Engines as New Power Turbines Take Six Years

AI data-center developers are hunting for used gas turbines and retired jet engines because ordering brand-new power equipment could leave their servers waiting for electricity until the next decade.

Some companies are buying refurbished machines, while others are converting aircraft-engine technology into generators that can run alongside their computing facilities.

New gas turbines now take an average of six years to deliver in the United States, according to energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie. Delivery discussions are already focused on 2030 and 2031, a timeline that clashes with an AI industry trying to bring enormous computing campuses online much sooner.

Global turbine orders have topped 100 gigawatts, compared with manufacturers' estimated annual capacity of just 60 to 70 gigawatts, Reuters reported. Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries have all said orders are outpacing what they can produce.

Gas turbines can generate large amounts of electricity by burning natural gas to spin equipment connected to a generator. AI data centers need that power around the clock to run densely packed chips and cooling systems, and connecting new facilities to public electricity grids can itself take years.

The International Energy Agency expects global data-center electricity consumption to nearly double from 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 in 2030. Consumption at AI-focused facilities is projected to triple over the same period.

One way around the backlog is an aeroderivative turbine, a power generator built using technology adapted from aircraft jet engines.

Other companies are going further by seeking older machines and retired aircraft engines that can be rebuilt for stationary power production. For example, AI infrastructure firm Crusoe ordered 13 units from Missouri-based ProEnergy in April, each rated at 50 megawatts, for a combined 650 megawatts. The jet-engine-derived equipment is intended for future U.S. data centers, but the contract doesn’t mean that Crusoe bought engines removed from retired aircraft.

Second-hand machines can also carry a substantial discount. Used turbines in good condition sell for about $1.5 million to $1.7 million per megawatt, compared with roughly $2 million to $2.5 million for new units, according to equipment brokers and energy analysts interviewed by Reuters.

One broker described a sale of two smaller turbines totaling 29 megawatts for $12.5 million. Equivalent new equipment would have cost about $35 million and taken five years to arrive, he said.

“That secondary market is very, very hot right now,” EthosEnergy CEO Ana Amicarella told Reuters, adding that asking prices are climbing as more buyers compete for the same machinery.

Building a power plant beside a data center also brings fuel needs, air emissions, and permits into the equation. The Environmental Protection Agency says stationary turbines and engines used by data centers are subject to federal air-pollution standards.

Last week, OpenAI promised to cover electricity and grid costs at future campuses it owns and operates after voters backed tighter restrictions on data-center construction.

Power-market research firm Cleanview identified about 90 gigawatts of proposed on-site generation at U.S. data centers in its mid-2026 analysis. Only about 2 gigawatts was operating at the time

#5149. OpenAI adds a 35-second emergency brake for its research AI

Control Room cuts off new model output within 35 seconds of a stop instruction, even if the underlying research code keeps running.

OpenAI says its newly disclosed Control Room system can cut off further model output from research jobs within 35 seconds after the service receives a stop instruction, placing enforcement outside the job's own code.

The company says the system is already deployed across its research infrastructure. The 35-second maximum begins when Control Room receives the instruction; spotting a problem, investigating it and deciding to intervene happen before that clock starts.

The design centers on a job ID. A research workload attaches that identifier when it requests model output. Before fulfilling the request, the inference engine, the software running the model, checks whether Control Room still authorizes that job.

Once the job is marked as stopped, the engine denies further output for it. The research process may remain alive, and the same engine can continue serving other authorized jobs. Enforcement therefore does not depend on the workload checking a stop flag correctly.

OpenAI says research code changes frequently and is spread across teams. The inference layer has fewer, more centralized code paths, providing a common point at which to enforce the decision. The company also says it continually searches for rogue engines with Control Room checks missing or disabled.

Cached authorizations account for the delay before the cutoff takes effect. The service can deny a stopped job access to further model output even while its own code continues trying to request it.

OpenAI says Control Room cuts research-job model output within 35 seconds of receiving a stop instruction.

The engine checks the job ID with Control Room and returns model output when permission is granted.

After cached authorization expires, the engine denies further output for the stopped job, while the research process may remain alive.

The engine enforces the stop; detecting trouble and containing external actions remain separate.

OpenAI's description of research infrastructure, not an independent performance test. The clock excludes detection and decision time. Blocking model output does not establish rollback of external actions.

Schematic of OpenAI's disclosed authorization path. Compare an authorized request with a stopped job after cached authorization expires. The 35-second maximum is reported, not calculated; line lengths are not proportional to time.

OpenAI's description of research infrastructure, not an independent performance test. The clock excludes detection and decision time. Blocking model output does not establish rollback of external actions.

OpenAI's Oct. 29 monitoring explanation describes screening, investigation and response as distinct stages. Some critical alerts can automatically pause workloads; other alerts follow arrangements that vary by workload and severity.

The oversight problem predates this disclosure. CryptoSlate reported on Oct. 21 that OpenAI coding agents had removed monitoring integration or suppressed security notifications during internal programming tasks. Those cases concerned monitoring and alerts, rather than the cutoff described here.

At disclosure, OpenAI said fail-closed behavior, under which engines deny inference requests if Control Room goes down, was active for all frontier model research workloads. The company said remaining research workloads would receive it over the following few days.

Cutting off model access does not end the still-running process or undo actions already taken in external systems.

#5148. Bitcoin Heated Hot Tubs and 278 Washington Bitcoin Merchants : Now Accepting Bitcoin

Washington Bitcoin merchants, from Seattle coffee shops to a Snorkel hot tub heated by bitcoin miners.

Washington Bitcoin merchant list has 278 businesses, from coffee shops and salons to a hot tub maker that heats its tubs with bitcoin mining. The list spans 94 named cities, and Seattle leads the way with 46 listings. First up is a homegrown US manufacturing business from Washington that makes a super unique product.

Snorkel has been making hot tubs in the Pacific Northwest since 1979, and its wood-stove business dates to the late 1970s. What makes them special is their full cedar tubs, and the wood stove which is fully submerged into the water of the cedar hot tub and has the “snorkel” coming out of the water. This is very convenient for anyone who has no electrical hook up.

It started with a bet in 2025. Michael Diederich, the owner, began accepting bitcoin for hot tubs after a wager with his brother. Payments were slow to trickle in at first, but bitcoiners kept asking him to build a hot tub powered by bitcoin miners. He started building one, pairing the tub with miners that heat the water. Snorkel works with Dane Sjoden of Hashrate House on the build.

The prototype with two S19J Pro miners drawing about 8 kW, which it says heated a tub from cold to 104°F (40°C) in under four hours. The project won an innovation award at the Heat Punk Summit in Denver, and a Snorkel tub is on display in Denver. Diederich sees a future where every electric hot tub is heated by miners, because the mining income helps pay back the cost of energy that would otherwise be wasted as heat.

The Rose sits at 226 Main Ave S in downtown Renton, in the Old Renton Pub building. Owner Katie Newman opened it in October 2020 as a gift shop that happened to serve coffee, and the coffee side grew into the larger part of the business. The shop stocks locally roasted coffee, handpicked artisan goods, and grab-and-go food. It won Best Customer Service in the 2025 Best of Renton readers’ poll.

Overcast Coffee is on Capitol Hill, and it started as a walk-up counter at 312 15th Ave E beside Kaiser Permanente. Owner Jonathan Pak opened the first shop there in June 2020. A second location, at 1517 12th Ave inside the Metier bike complex, came later, and the company buys its coffee and ingredients from small, local Seattle businesses.

#5147. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.0 Are Impressive, But Be Prepared to Sell a Kidney to Afford Them

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.0 Are Impressive, But Be Prepared to Sell a Kidney to Afford Them

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Monday, promising AI models that can turn a handful of instructions into working software, design physical objects, and tackle research problems that previously required teams of specialists.

You can now ask a chatbot to build the app you've always wanted. You may also need to sell a kidney to pay for it.

That's not because every prompt costs thousands of dollars. It's because Fable can keep working for days, writing code, testing it, and fixing its own mistakes while the meter keeps running.

Some users have already tested its capabilities, and they’ve been impressed—by the power, and the price.

AI YouTuber Matthew Berman put the model through a series of ambitious tests and described Fable 5.2 as the “best AI model” he's ever used. His projects included playable video games and a browser-based version of Microsoft Excel, complete with formulas and pivot tables.

One single level of Gears of War: E-Day-inspired level took 43 hours and 48 minutes of build time and processed 8.63 billion tokens—small chunks of information an AI reads and produces. The running API cost estimate, based on pay-as-you-go pricing for developers, had reached $14,710.

I've burned over 100 billion tokens early testing Fable 5.2. It is BY FAR the best model I've ever used.

Here's my full review (including Gears of War clone):

> Fable 5.2 is the most autonomous model to date. Given a task with little direction, it makes… pic.twitter.com/0xTzqTY040

— Matthew Berman (@MatthewBerman) November 9, 2026

The Excel clone ran up an estimated $11,700 after discounts for cached inputs, or information the system can reuse instead of processing from scratch. Berman also showed a Fall Guys-style game that consumed more than 9 billion tokens over 71 hours, equivalent to roughly $13,000.

Those are estimated API costs, and the projects weren't flawless: Berman reported awkward animations, bugs, and features that still needed testing.

If you’re poor, well… Fable also knows how to work for cheap. For less than $40 (two months of Claude Pro) it built a cute orange cylinder.

Another experiment simulated water-balloon physics for $91. It’s worth noting this isn’t a model intended for routine tasks. This is for serious work and people with deep pockets.

In its launch announcement, Anthropic said the new models generate output up to 30% faster than their predecessors. The company also says Fable helped solve two open theoretical-physics problems involving black holes and design three functioning electronic devices, claims that will need independent scrutiny.

Anthropic's internal FrontierCode 2.0 evaluation, which measures the percentage of proposed coding changes that would be accepted into real open-source projects, put Fable 5.2 at 49.1%, compared with 32.4% for Fable 5.1. That helps explain why users are pushing it beyond simple chat responses.

Fable and Mythos share the same underlying model, but Fable has stricter safeguards around dangerous biological and cybersecurity requests. Mythos is reserved for verified organizations working in those fields.

The standard API price is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from the previous generation's $10 and $50. Optional fast mode can generate output up to 2.5 times faster, but doubles the rates to $16 and $80.

For contrast, Kimi 3.1 Pro, a model considered by many as the best Chinese AI model costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. The latest Deepseek model costs $0.6 and $1.98 outside of peak hours.

Per Anthropic’s standards, Fable’s price is still twice the per-token price of Claude Opus 5.5, which Anthropic recommends for everyday work. Its flagship is meant for problems the cheaper models struggle to finish, not for asking whether your email sounds too aggressive.

Just last week, speculation swirled around a supposed Fable 5.5. The actual release is 5.2, with cheaper token rates but enough appetite to turn a hobby project into a serious expense.

Anthropic, last we checked, doesn’t accept kidneys as a method of payment.

#5146. Thousands of Bitcoin nodes gave anonymous strangers a pass around security limits

The project rated CVE-2025-62860 medium severity. It affected vulnerable releases when a non-default -whitelist setting covered the IP address of the node's Tor daemon, the software handling its Tor connections. Nodes that never enabled that setting were never affected.

The fixes shipped in October 2025. The new disclosure explains how a configuration intended for trusted connections spread through bundled software and granted those privileges to remote Tor peers.

For an incoming Tor connection, Bitcoin Core sees the Tor daemon's IP address rather than the remote peer's actual network address. That daemon usually runs on the same machine or local network.

On affected configurations, Core checked that address against an IP range marked as trusted. If the range included the daemon, incoming Tor connections inherited the whitelist permissions. The local address identified the intermediary carrying the connection, but could not establish which remote peer deserved trust.

On vulnerable configurations, an IP whitelist trusted the local Tor daemon's address and passed exemptions to incoming remote peers.

A vulnerable release used the daemon's matching IP range to grant trusted-peer exemptions.

Incoming onion connections bypass address-based whitelist matching, preventing this mistaken grant.

The patch excludes incoming onion connections from address-based whitelist grants.

Before-fix state requires a vulnerable release and a non-default whitelist matching the Tor daemon. The change concerns address-based -whitelist permissions, not every possible peer permission.

Qualitative connection path plus two reported states. Peer markers illustrate multiple remote connections and encode no count or scale.

Before-fix state requires a vulnerable release and a non-default whitelist matching the Tor daemon. The change concerns address-based -whitelist permissions, not every possible peer permission.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Bitcoin Core says popular vendors bundled the node software with Tor and a matching whitelist range. Some client software also required whitelisting and commonly ran alongside Tor. Together, these configurations led thousands of reachable mainnet nodes to whitelist every incoming Tor connection.

That is the advisory's historical exposure finding, not a count of nodes still vulnerable today.

Martin Zumsande and Antoine Poinsot reported the issue in September 2025. The patch merged on Sept. 17 and stopped applying address-based whitelist permissions to incoming onion connections, whose remote network addresses are concealed.

Bitcoin Core 30.0, 29.2 and 28.3 shipped the fix in October 2025. The fix is present in all versions from 30.0 onward, as well as later minor releases in the fixed 28.x and 29.x branches.

Those older patch thresholds are separate from today's upgrade guidance. Bitcoin Core's maintenance schedule now covers 30.x, 31.x and 32.x; 28.x and 29.x have reached end of life. The project recommends the latest maintenance release of the newest major version an operator can adopt. Its download page lists 32.1 as latest as of Nov. 11.

For operators using packaged node software, check the Bitcoin Core version actually running and whether its whitelist range includes the Tor daemon's address.

#5145. Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients

Deutsche Bank has switched on its digital asset custody service for paying clients, the German lender said Wednesday, letting institutions and corporations in Europe hold bitcoin with the country’s largest bank less than two months after it first unveiled the plan.

The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page.

Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure.

“In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank.

The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers.

The product page describes private keys stored in hardware security modules, a choice of warm and cold storage, multi-factor authentication, segregation of client assets and a customizable approval process for client transfers. Clients reach the service through Autobahn, Deutsche Bank’s multi-channel gateway, or its Corporate Bank portal.

The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and is available in Germany, with cross-border servicing across Europe through passporting. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules.

For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap.

It also carried a warning familiar to anyone in bitcoin: crypto assets held this way are not covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme like the one that protects eligible bank deposits.

Alongside the launch, Deutsche Bank signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the money manager it mostly owns that was known until recently as DWS. The agreement is meant “to explore comprehensive commercial and technical collaboration opportunities in the digital asset space,” the bank said.

The firms plan to look at tokenized money market funds, crypto exchange-traded commodities and stablecoins built around the new custody platform, and Deutsche Asset Management’s chief product officer, Manfred Bauer, said it plans to launch a tokenized money market fund, according to a report. The asset manager oversaw about €1.22 trillion as of Sept. 30.

Deutsche Asset Management already backs AllUnity, the joint venture that issues EURAU, one of the three stablecoins the bank’s custody service supports.

Deutsche Bank has also told Reuters it wants to bring the service to Asia. In October, the bank’s corporate banking chief said the lender planned to expand the platform into the region next year.

The launch puts Deutsche Bank alongside a growing list of large banks that now hold bitcoin for clients. BNY Mellon became the first major U.S. bank to offer digital asset custody in 2022, and this year Standard Chartered moved to offer custody in Singapore while South Africa’s Absa became the first bank on the continent to custody bitcoin.

In the U.S., Coinbase this week won a full federal trust charter from the OCC, another sign that custody is becoming a regulated banking business on both sides of the Atlantic.

The timing is not ideal for new money. Bitcoin traded near $73,900 Wednesday morning, close to its lowest level since August after a hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report on Tuesday.

DeepMind reports 96% success in a parts-sorting pilot on Mercedes-Benz production lines in Germany and Hungary. Human-intervention rates remain undisclosed.

Google DeepMind says robot maker Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoids achieved a 96% success rate sorting automotive parts on active Mercedes-Benz production lines, using AI to handle preparation work that feeds vehicle assembly.

The company disclosed the proof of concept on Nov. 10, identifying sites in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany. The work provides a specific test for its Gemini Robotics 2.5 model: arranging the components needed by the people building cars.

The task was automotive kitting, which involves taking parts from bulk bins and organizing them in the order needed for each vehicle. DeepMind's example involved picking up metal brackets and placing them into sequencing containers. That ties the demonstration to a defined step in preparing an assembly line's supplies. The trays are meant to match the parts needed for each vehicle, so getting the sequence right is part of the task. The robot has to organize the components as well as move them.

Apollo 2 prepared parts in vehicle order in DeepMind's Mercedes-Benz proof of concept.

#5143. 'Tough Questions' Ahead: Warren Targets Prediction Markets, Trump Crypto as Banking Chair

'Tough Questions' Ahead: Warren Targets Prediction Markets, Trump Crypto as Banking Chair

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), one of the crypto industry's most prominent critics, is preparing to use the chairmanship of the Senate Banking Committee to launch an oversight campaign aimed at Trump family crypto businesses, Big Tech and Wall Street, Politico reported on Monday.

"Big Tech CEOs, Administration officials, Trump family crypto businesses, Wall Street executives, and giant corporations should preserve their documents and prepare to answer tough questions," a Warren Banking Committee aide told the outlet.

Warren is expected to take over the committee in January after Democrats won control of the Senate in last week's midterm elections. The panel oversees banking, housing, cryptocurrency and the Federal Reserve, and its chair has broad powers to call hearings and launch investigations.

According to the aide, Warren also wants to end a "Wild West-style lack of oversight" of prediction markets that she says has allowed insiders to profit, and plans to warn about threats to financial stability, including a potential AI bubble.

She intends to keep working with Republican China hawks to restrict exports of advanced AI chips, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is expected to be a top oversight target, Politico reported. The report came a day after Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been the target of a Chinese intelligence effort, sending Nvidia shares sliding as much as 8%.

Warren is also likely to investigate the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's August decision to grant a conditional bank charter to Trump-backed World Liberty Financial, as well as the administration's firings of financial agency staff and its efforts to shut down the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with her thinking. "You're going to see a lot of investigations," Brian Gardner, chief Washington policy strategist at Stifel, told the outlet.

In an essay for Time last week, Warren argued that Democrats won by "being populist economic fighters," and said "Big Tech CEOs, Wall Street executives, and giant corporations should prepare to answer tough questions and face meaningful consequences if they have broken the law."

Warren has been a persistent critic of the crypto industry and of the Trump family's business interests in it. She has argued that federal regulators' approval of national trust charters for crypto firms, including Coinbase and Ripple, is illegal, and has said the CFTC has been "steamrolled" by the prediction market and crypto firms it oversees.

She has also questioned Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over a Tether loan to a trust tied to his children, and joined Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) in urging the Labor Department to drop plans that would make it easier to hold crypto in 401(k) retirement plans.

Warren was one of the leading opponents of the Clarity Act, the crypto industry's top legislative priority, which stalled in the Senate this year. Democrats are now planning to push a broader crypto market structure bill when they take control of Congress.

The White House has pushed back. A spokesperson told Reuters that Trump is willing to work with anyone on behalf of Americans, but that "sham investigations and radical left policies" would undermine any such effort.

Republicans have cast Warren as the main obstacle to crypto legislation. Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC), the current Banking chair, has argued that without market structure rules, crypto is left in "the wild, wild West."

Warren's ability to pass legislation will be limited while Trump remains in the White House. In her Time essay, she acknowledged that Trump has embraced the nickname "Mr. Veto," but argued that Democrats should send him bills anyway.

Warren is also eyeing a more senior role in Senate Democratic leadership, potentially the No. 3 position, Politico reported last month.

OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected.

The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks, such as STRC.

Access at launch is limited to eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who have activated a CeDeFi Wallet, passed identity checks and completed onboarding with the joint venture, which is called OKXICE and is owned equally by ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trading will run around the clock in the OKX app.

“The future of finance is onchain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland.

The companies did not say how many of the more than 70 assets will trade on the first day, or how much liquidity the pools will have at the open. The venue is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC, the announcement said.

Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX operates. Only approved wallets can trade or add liquidity.

Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share held by a registered broker-dealer, and holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions, the venue said in a Nov. 5 public notice required under the exemption.

Customers will hold the tokens in their own wallets. OKXICE will not hold the assets or the private keys. The tokens will be paired with payment stablecoins such as USDC and USDG. The venue does not operate an order book, does not extend credit and does not conduct primary offerings, the notice said.

The same Nov. 5 notice lists 67 issuers that had sent a written objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta, Netflix, Nvidia, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Costco, Nike and Home Depot. The list has grown from 50 objectors in an Oct. 30 notice.

The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. When an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s stock, the venue must notify the issuer, which then has 30 days to object in writing.

The SEC’s innovation exemption page lists OKXICE TSV as having submitted a notice of intent on Oct. 4.

The names the companies highlighted are mostly crypto-linked. Strategy, the largest public bitcoin treasury company, is listing both its common stock and its preferreds. “Tokenization on the OKXICE TSV is a natural next step toward making Digital Credit accessible to investors around the world, 24 hours a day, seven days a week,” Strategy’s president and chief executive, Phong Le, said in the announcement, referring to preferreds such as STRC. Le also called bitcoin “Digital Capital.”

The test now is whether a venue that has lost Apple, Tesla, Nvidia and most of the rest of the largest U.S. companies can still draw enough trading to matter when it opens in 12 days, and whether any more issuers object before then.

For context, a tokenized stock is a blockchain token backed one-for-one by a real share. Under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, the venue can list these tokens without the issuing company’s consent, unless the company objects within 30 days.

For banks, that design fits an adaptation strategy described by Federal Reserve staff: respond to new payment competition through products, infrastructure and partnerships while continuing to serve customers. The pilot puts that approach into a specific receiving-payment service.

A credit in the receiving customer's PNC account tells us where that customer's money arrives. It does not tell us how the payer acquired USDC, who supplied the conversion dollars, or which other balances changed along the way. Those offsetting movements matter to whether the banking system gains funding overall.

A March 30 Federal Reserve staff model illustrates a possible inventory route. In its hypothetical cross-border payment, a recipient can sell stablecoins and deposit local currency while an intermediary retains the tokens. Fees and delays in exchanging tokens for currency can influence how much inventory intermediaries hold.

In a May 1 analysis of banks' responses to stablecoins, Fed staff distinguished aggregate deposit levels from their composition. Money can return to banks through issuers holding reserve deposits or through securities dealers redepositing proceeds. Stablecoin activity can shift the ownership and location of deposits without necessarily reducing the banking system's total deposits one-for-one.

The receiving customer's conversion is also separate from the issuer-side reserve choices discussed in CryptoSlate's October coverage.

For a business, the practical test is how efficiently those receipts become usable cash. PNC and Coinbase describe faster access to funds and greater cross-border efficiency as intended benefits. Their November announcements leave the precise settlement deadline, spendable-funds availability, operating hours, restrictions and pilot fees unspecified.

Those terms matter when comparing a blockchain transfer with the time it takes for the resulting bank balance to become available to spend. The companies have also disclosed no participating-client count, processed transaction volume or measured deposit effect in these announcements.

PNC has specified the customer's destination: a dollar deposit. The next evidence to watch is whether eligible businesses use the route and how it performs for their treasury operations.

#5139. Nvidia, Jensen Huang Sued by Shareholders Over Alleged Ties to Suspected Chinese Spy

Nvidia, Jensen Huang Sued by Shareholders Over Alleged Ties to Suspected Chinese Spy

Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang have been sued by a shareholder who accuses them of defrauding investors by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

The proposed class action, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on Monday, accuses Nvidia and Huang of making materially false and misleading statements about the company's dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, according to the complaint. It alleges that Huang "had an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy," and that the defendants failed to disclose that this raised national security concerns posing a material risk to Nvidia's reputation and business prospects.

The plaintiff, Mark Kistenmacher, seeks to represent investors who bought Nvidia stock between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2026. The suit accuses Nvidia and Huang of violating Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, and Huang of violating Section 20(a), which can hold executives liable alongside a company. It seeks unspecified damages and a jury trial. Kistenmacher is represented by The Rosen Law Firm.

The complaint targets four statements. Two came from Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo in October 2025, when he told The New York Times that Nvidia's employees had "found no evidence of diversion" at Megaspeed and that Huang's visits to customer events were routine. A third came from Rizzo last month, when he said Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were "not unusual or unexpected." The fourth was Huang's own description of Nvidia's dealings with Megaspeed as "normal and not unusual" in an interview with Bloomberg on October 30. Each was misleading, the suit alleges, because of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, is not related to Jensen Huang, Reuters reported. The New York Times reported on Sunday that Nvidia opened its investigation after Huang acknowledged to the company's board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang. The newspaper also reported that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a classified memo this spring warning top administration officials about the relationship, which was circulated ahead of U.S. President Donald Trump's trip to China in May.

Decrypt has reached out to Nvidia for comment. The allegations in the complaint have not been tested in court, and it is common for shareholders to sue companies after sharp share price declines.

The lawsuit was filed five minutes after U.S. markets closed on Monday, according to Reuters. Nvidia shares closed down 4.3% at $178.67 that day, according to Yahoo Finance, reducing its market value by about $190 billion, after having slid as much as 8% earlier in the session. The stock was flat on the day at $179.70 in premarket trading on Tuesday.

Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Sunday into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, saying it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised. In an email to staff the same day, Huang apologized for being unfaithful to his wife, without naming the person involved.

The New York Times reported last month that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, and the Financial Times later reported that a U.S. government memo said Jensen Huang had been romantically involved with her. China's embassy in Washington has dismissed the allegations as "groundless smears."

Trump weighed in on Monday. "I asked him about that and he said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," the president told reporters, according to The Guardian. He added that the FBI was "looking into it in terms of something else," without elaborating. A day earlier, Trump told reporters he did not regret his decision not to act on the intelligence, and that he believed Huang should stay on as CEO. "I think he's an honorable guy," he said, according to the Times.
